MRI of left knee with -Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, CO T2W FS, AX T2W FS

Findings:
> The contour of anterior and posterior cruciate ligaments appearing within normal limit
> High signal intensity in medial and lateral meniscus without significant extending to the surface, probably due to myxoid degeneration
> Bony fragement in posterior knee joint, suspecious of loose body.
> Spur formation in left knee joint and patella with subchondral edema and cysts, indicating osteoarthritis.
> Full thickness cartilage loss of patella, suggestive of chondromalacia
> Large amount of joint effusion with suprapatellar bursitis 

Impression:
1. Osteoarthritis of left knee joint
2. Suspect intra-articular loose body in posterior knee joint
3. Myxoid degeneration of medial and lateral meniscus
4. Chondromalacia of patella cartilage
5. Large amount of joint effusion with suprapatellar bursitis 

Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation and further evaluation.

MRI of right Knee with 
-Locator, SG PD FatSat, SG T2W FS, SG T1W, AX T2W FS, CO T2W FS



> Spur formation and subchondral bone marrow edema of knee and irregular thining of intra-articular cartilage and some intra-articular loose bodies, reflecting osteoarthritis of knee, more severe at patellofemoral joint and lateral femorotibial joint .
> The contour of ACL in a straight line and increase signal intensity inside on F/S T2WI, in favor of grade 1 injury or mucoid degeneration.
> The contour of PCL appears to be within normal, no abnormal signal intensity is noted.
> Small size of medial meniscal root with increased signal  on F/S T2WI, R/O tear.
    Linear signal intensity in anterior horn of lateral meniscus, without significant extending into the surface, in favor of  grade 2 intrasubstance signal , maybe due to degeneration.
> Both medial & lateral collateral ligaments appear to be within normal.
> Joint effusion and suprapatellar bursitis with suprapatellar and medial plicae; hypertrophy of the synovium, indicative of synovitis. Small Baker's cyst
> Increased fat stranding and minimal fluid accumulation located along the pes anserinus, R/O Anserine bursitis

Impression: 
1. Osteoarthritis of right knee, more prominent at lateral compartment with grade 4 chondromalacia.
2. R/O medial meniscal root tear; degeneration of lateral meniscus.
3. Synovitis of right knee and suprapatellar bursitis and patellar plicae.
4. Small Baker's cyst and anserine bursitis.
5. Grade 1 injury or degeneration of ACL.
Suggest correlation with clinical manifestation

Interprétation : 
Il y a un petit épanchement intra-articulaire. Pas de kyste de Baker significatif avec un liséré de liquide au sein du récessus poplité. 
En corrélation avec les radiographies du genou droit, suspicion d’un ossicule méniscal au sein de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne mesurant 7-8mm de diamètre avec déchirure radiaire transfixiante à la jonction de la corne postérieure et de la racine postérieure de même qu’au niveau de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne avec extrusion significative du corps méniscal de façon associée. Ceci est nouveau dans l’intervalle. Stabilité d’une déchirure longitudinale horizontale centrée au corps du ménisque interne s’étendant légèrement aux cornes postérieures et antérieures et à la surface articulaire inférieure. 
Également dans l’intervalle, il y a progression significative des changements dégénératifs au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne avec perte transfixiante des surfaces chondrales, principalement aux surfaces portantes et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ostéophytes marginaux modérés. 
Le ligament collatéral interne est intact sans déchirure. 
Légers changements de signal au sein de la corne antérieure du ménisque externe suggérant des changements de nature mucoïde dégénératifs. Pas de franche déchirure notée. 
Changements dégénératifs légers à modérés au compartiment fémoro-tibial externe avec atténuation/fissure chondrale partielle à la surface portante et petits ostéophytes marginaux associés. 
Le complexe ligamentaire collatéral externe est intact sans déchirure. 
Les ligaments croisés antérieur et postérieur sont intacts sans déchirure. Petit kyste intra-osseux réactionnel sous l’insertion distale du ligament croisé postérieur. 
L’alignement patellofémoral est préservé. Changements dégénératifs modérés à sévères au compartiment patellofémoral, plus marqués le long de la facette patellaire externe et apex patellaire avec fissures chondrales transfixiantes et changements sous-chondraux réactionnels associés. Ceci a minimalement progressé dans l’intervalle. Petits ostéophytes marginaux. 
Légère tendinose à l’insertion distale du tendon du quadriceps et de façon plus diffuse au niveau du tendon patellaire. Pas de franche déchirure notée. 
Conclusion : 
Nouvelle déchirure radiale transfixiante à la jonction de la corne postérieure et de la racine postérieure de même qu’au niveau de la corne postérieure du ménisque interne avec extrusion secondaire marquée du corps méniscal tel que détaillé ci-haut. Suspicion d’un ossicule méniscal à la jonction de la corne postérieure et de la racine postérieure du ménisque interne, en corrélation avec une radiographie du genou droit. 
Progression dans l’intervalle des changements dégénératifs/chondropathie tricompartimentaux, sévères au compartiment fémoro-tibial interne et modérés à sévères au compartiment patellofémoral plus marqués le long de la facette patellaire externe de l’apex patellaire.

FINDINGS:

Fractures:
Known mildly comminuted undisplaced avulsion fracture of the tibial tuberosity involving the distal ACL insertion, anteriorly the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, as well as posteriorly the tibial insertion of both the posterior horn of medial and lateral menisci. The fracture involves the central portion of the medial tibial plateau articular surface anteriorly and posteriorly with articular surface collapse of 3 mm anteriorly and 5 mm posteriorly, as well as a step deformity of up to 2 mm posteriorly.
Small mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the lateral corner of lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
Small mild osteochondral impaction at the anterior lateral weightbearing aspect of lateral femoral condyle.
There is associated bone marrow edema associated with these fractures.

Joint alignment:
Mild widening of the medial femorotibial joint space. Otherwise preserved articular alignment.

Degenerative changes:
None.

Bone marrow signal:
Additional small area of bone marrow edema on the medial side of medial femoral condyle without evidence of associated fracture.

Anterior cruciate ligament: The distal bony avulsion with laxity of the ACL, showing some internal high T2 signal changes compatible with additional low-grade partial ligamentous tear.
Posterior cruciate ligament: Intact with mild laxity.
Medial collateral ligament: Complete tear of the superficial portion at the mid to distal third. Moderate grade partial tear of the deep meniscal femoral and meniscal tibial components with partial meniscocapsular separation of the medial meniscal body.
Lateral collateral ligament complex: Low-grade sprain of the proximal lateral collateral ligament. The other associated structures are intact.

Medial meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes of the meniscal body, with evidence of small horizontal oblique tear extending to the femoral surface. No other significant tear. Bony avulsion of the posterior horn root insertion as detailed above.
Lateral meniscus: Mild nonspecific signal changes at the anterior horn compatible with low-grade tearing. Evidence of small Wrisberg rip-type longitudinal tear of the periphery of the posterior horn. Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury. There is a bony avulsion of the anterior horn and posterior horn root insertion sites.

Extensor tendons: Normal.
Patellar retinacula: Moderate grade partial tear of the medial retinaculum.
Pes anserinus: Normal.

Posteromedial and posterolateral corner: Diffuse signal change and mild thickening of the distal semimembranosus tendon compatible with low to moderate grade partial tearing.
Complete tear of the inferior meniscal popliteal fascicle compatible with posterior lateral corner injury.

Joint effusion: Large joint effusion.
Baker cyst: None.

Other significant findings:
None.

CONCLUSION:
*Comminuted mildly displaced avulsion fracture of the tibial spine with mild comminution, including the distal insertion of the ACL, the anterior horn root insertion of the lateral meniscus, and posterior horn root insertion zone of the medial and lateral menisci. Intra-articular fracture extension involving the central portion of the medial tibial plateau with small gap/step as described.
*Small mildly displaced lateral corner fracture of the lateral tibial plateau [Segond fracture].
*Small osteochondral impaction fracture of the lateral corner of lateral femoral condyle.
*High-grade tear of the medial collateral ligament.
*Low-grade partial tear/sprain of the anterior cruciate ligament and lateral collateral ligament.
*Additional low-grade tears involving the medial and lateral menisci as described.
*Moderate grade partial tear of the medial patellar retinaculum.
*Posteromedial and posterolateral corner injuries as described.
*Large joint effusion.

Exam Type: MRI KNEE LEFT WO CONTRAST
Exam Date and Time: [DATE] [TIME]
Indication: 64-year-old with progressive left knee pain related to "wear and tear". Evaluate for cartilage loss. Evaluate for meniscus tear.
Comparison: No recent left lower extremity imaging available for comparison.

TECHNIQUE:
MRI of the left knee is acquired in 3 anatomic planes at 1.2 Tesla using a local extremity receiver coil and a noncontrast protocol.

FINDINGS:

OSSEOUS STRUCTURES:
Osseous and articular alignment at the left knee are normal.
No fracture. No focal osseous contusion.
No evidence for a recent pivot shift mechanism.

JOINT SPACE:
There is a small left knee effusion.
There is a minimal, partially ruptured Baker's cyst.
No intra-articular bodies.

MEDIAL COMPARTMENT:
Medial meniscus: There is a complex tear of the medial meniscus body and posterior horn with a dominant oblique undersurface component and a smaller inner margin radial component at the junction posterior horn and posterior root. There is moderate subsequent medial meniscus extrusion.
Medial compartment cartilage: There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss all along the weightbearing region of the medial femoral condyle, with focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the medial femoral margin.
There is partial-thickness cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

LATERAL COMPARTMENT:
Lateral meniscus: The lateral meniscus shows normal morphology and signal with no tear.
Lateral compartment cartilage: Articular cartilage throughout the lateral tibiofemoral compartment is normal.

PATELLOFEMORAL COMPARTMENT:
There is a small region of focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge, with more diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss extending along the medial patellar facet.
There is diffuse partial-thickness cartilage loss with deep chondral fissuring at the central femoral trochlea.

CRUCIATE LIGAMENTS:
Anterior cruciate ligament (ACL): Normal with both bundles intact.
Posterior cruciate ligament (PCL): Normal morphology and signal.

COLLATERAL LIGAMENTS & POSTEROLATERAL CORNER:
Medial collateral ligament (MCL): The MCL is bowed from medial meniscus extrusion, but intact.
Lateral collateral ligament (LCL) complex: The fibular-collateral ligament and anterolateral ligament are normal.
Posterolateral corner structures: Intact stabilizers.

EXTENSOR MECHANISM:
Distal quadriceps tendon: Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with intrasubstance degeneration at its patellar attachment and mild enthesopathy. No high-grade quadriceps tear.
Patella tendon: Normal morphology and signal with no tear or degeneration.
Medial patellofemoral ligament (MPFL) and patellar retinacula: Normal.
Patellofemoral tracking: No significant soft tissue edema in Hoffa's fat.
A TT-TG distance is normal at 7 mm.

MUSCLES/TENDONS:
The distal iliotibial band and biceps femoris are normal.
The distal semimembranosus is normal.

SOFT TISSUES:
Neurovascular structures in the popliteal fossa are normal.
Subcutaneous soft tissues are normal. No soft tissue mass.

IMPRESSION:

1. Extensive complex medial meniscus tear with a dominant oblique undersurface component at its body and posterior horn, moderate medial meniscus extrusion, and high-grade cartilage loss on the medial femoral condyle with low-grade cartilage loss at the medial tibial margin.

2. Focal full-thickness cartilage loss at the patellar median ridge with high-grade partial-thickness cartilage loss at the central femoral trochlea.

3. Moderate degenerative hypertrophic distal quadriceps tendinopathy, with mild enthesopathy.

4. Small left knee effusion with a minimal ruptured Baker's cyst.
